Executive pitch

Make existing repositories ready for the AI engineering era

“The next barrier to AI-powered development isn't the coding assistant. It's the context our repositories provide.”

RepoReady AI assesses how well an engineering repository supports AI-assisted development, identifies missing instructions and context, proposes developer-reviewed improvements, and measures progress through reassessment.

Select a repository → Assess readiness → Understand the gaps → Improve guidance → Reassess.

Question 5 · Copy-ready

The problem

AI coding assistants are transforming how we develop software. But are our existing codebases prepared to get the best from them?

In large, complex repositories, architecture knowledge is often scattered, build and test instructions are unclear, coding conventions are undocumented, and AI-specific guidance may be missing.

Developers spend time repeatedly explaining the codebase, while AI agents lack the context needed to make reliable, consistent changes.

We have AI-powered development tools, but no consistent way to measure and improve whether our repositories are ready for them.

RepoReady AI closes that gap.

Question 6 · Copy-ready solution

The solution

RepoReady AI — Is your codebase AI-ready?

RepoReady AI is an intelligent repository readiness assistant that helps Aviva engineering teams assess, improve and maintain their codebases for AI-powered development.

The experience is simple: Select a repository. Discover what's missing. Make it AI-ready.

1CONNECT

A developer selects an approved Azure DevOps repository through a Power Apps portal and requests an assessment.

2ASSESS

An approved pipeline or lightweight scanner checks AI instructions, architecture context, build/test guidance, conventions and safeguards against explicit criteria.

3UNDERSTAND

Copilot/Agent Builder uses structured findings and approved guidance to explain the gaps, supporting evidence and improvement priorities.

4IMPROVE

The agent drafts missing documentation or repository instructions for developer review; no changes are committed automatically.

5PROVE

Reassessment shows which defined readiness gaps were resolved and which remain open.

Value to Aviva

RepoReady AI can help teams get more value from existing Copilot investment, reduce repeated codebase discovery, improve onboarding and establish consistent standards for AI-assisted engineering. The readiness score reflects documented criteria; it is not a guarantee of AI-generated code quality.

How we'll build it

Azure DevOps hosts approved repositories and optionally runs a scanner; Power Apps provides the interface; Power Automate can coordinate assessment requests and status updates where approved integrations exist; SharePoint stores reports and guidance; Agent Builder / Copilot explains findings and drafts recommendations.

Hackathon scope: One approved or synthetic sample repository, one assessment, prioritised AI recommendations and a before-and-after comparison, without touching production repositories.

Architecture · Technical flow

How the components connect

1 · Developer → Power AppsSelect an approved repository and initiate a readiness assessment.
↓
2 · Power Automate (conditional integration)Pass a validated assessment request to an approved DevOps endpoint / workflow. Requires connector, authentication and permissions.
↓
3 · Azure DevOps Pipeline + Readiness ScannerRead permitted repository files, run deterministic checks, produce evidence-backed structured JSON.
↓
4 · SharePoint Assessment StoreSave assessment JSON, report, checklist and approved reference guidance.
↓
5 · Copilot / Agent BuilderExplain results, answer questions and draft prioritised improvements from accessible assessment information.
↓
6 · Power Apps Results + Developer ReviewShow score, findings and proposed changes; human approves improvements; rerun scanner to compare.

Two-day hackathon

Build something judges can see working

StageDemonstration
Day 1Create a small synthetic repository and readiness checklist; implement scanner producing JSON; store results in SharePoint or local demo artifacts.
Day 2Present results through Power Apps or a simple approved dashboard; use Agent Builder on accessible findings; draft one improvement; reassess and compare.
Live story“Before: missing guidance. Agent identifies gaps. Developer approves proposed instructions. After: readiness improves against transparent checks.”

Fallback if integration is blocked: Use a pre-generated assessment file and approved sample data in SharePoint. Demonstrate AI interpretation and improvement recommendations without pretending the live DevOps connection works.

Delivery realism

Dependencies, safeguards and success measures

  • Access: Repository reading and pipeline execution require approved Azure DevOps credentials, policies and connectivity.
  • Agent capability: Basic Agent Builder is primarily conversational; arbitrary external actions may require Copilot Studio or another approved integration.
  • Data protection: Do not export secrets, proprietary source or sensitive configuration into unapproved stores or AI knowledge sources.
  • Human control: Generated documentation is proposed for review; no autonomous commits or production changes.
  • Success measures: Percentage of readiness criteria met, number of evidence-backed gaps closed, time to produce assessment and developer feedback on usefulness.
  • Limit: Improved readiness documentation does not itself prove faster delivery or safer AI code. Those outcomes need separate testing.
One repo. One clear readiness baseline. One actionable improvement. One measurable reassessment.
